name: Rocco Forte The Balmoral, Edinburgh
positioning: Rocco Forte's The Balmoral, a hotel built in 1902 for the North British Railway at 1 Princes Street, where Edinburgh's Old Town meets the New Town, with the SCOTCH whisky bar, Palm Court afternoon tea and the Irene Forte Spa
best_for: Travelers who want a central Edinburgh base between the Old Town and the New Town

facts.text: The hotel is at 1 Princes Street in Edinburgh, where the Old Town meets the New Town.
The hotel was built in 1902 for the North British Railway company.
The Old Town and the Royal Mile are just on the other side of Waverley station.
During Hogmanay, the hotel's clock marks the turning of the year precisely on time.
Guests are welcomed with bespoke Balmoral tartan, and the hotel features classic Scottish art.
The suites were designed by Olga Polizzi to reflect the Scottish landscape.
Brasserie Prince pairs classic French cooking with Scottish produce.
Bar Prince has cornflower-blue leather chairs and a bar with copper barware.
The Irene Forte Spa draws its inspiration from Sicily.
Family Rooms are two interconnecting rooms with two bedrooms.
The Bowes-Lyon Suite is named for the Queen Mother, a former patron of the hotel.

highlights.text: The hotel's clock tower is set three minutes fast so guests and railway passengers don't miss their trains.
SCOTCH, the hotel's whisky bar, holds over 500 Scottish whiskies in a hand-crafted, oak-panelled cabinet.
J.K. Rowling finished the final Harry Potter book in the suite now named after her.
The Palm Court serves afternoon tea under palm trees, a glass dome and a Venetian chandelier.
The Irene Forte Spa has an indoor lap pool.

considerations.text: There is no dress code, but the hotel asks guests not to wear sportswear, shorts or beach shoes in its restaurants.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing that reflects the hotel's exclusive positioning.
WhataHotel notes the historic building may have traditional room layouts.
